title: Rules 7–8: action and the reader as key
summary: Gate the page on something a reader can do — and let their own life supply the decryption, not a footnote from you.

blocks.title: Toward a verb; toward their life
blocks.body: The last two rules decide what the page is for. If it only invites recognition gossip, privacy and teaching both fail. If you ship a decoder ring, you undid the encoding.

blocks.heading: 7. Gate everything on action
blocks.body:
The page exists so a reader can do something differently: ask a better question, refuse a bad default, redesign a handoff, leave a paper trail. If the allegory only invites gossip or recognition ("I know who that is"), it failed the privacy craft and the teaching craft at once.

Write toward a verb. End near an action the reader owns — not toward a reveal about people they do not.

items.label: Name the verb
items.detail: Ask, refuse, redesign, document, escalate, leave — something concrete.

items.label: Place it near the end
items.detail: Recognition without a next step is entertainment, not education.

items.label: Strip gossip bait
items.detail: If a line only helps someone guess who you meant, cut it.

blocks.heading: 8. Let the reader's own life be the key
blocks.body:
You are not shipping a decoder ring. The useful decryption happens when the reader's memory supplies the entities that match your relationships. That is intentional: the people who need the lesson already have the context; strangers get a transferable pattern without a roster.

If you feel the urge to add a footnote that "really" explains who was who, you are undoing the encoding. Trust the reader who has lived something adjacent. Everyone else was never your audience for the private layer.

nodes.title: Page publishes
nodes.detail: No roster, no mapping table, no wink that only one friend can read.

nodes.title: Reader decrypts
nodes.detail: Their life supplies entities. Strangers keep the pattern only.

blocks.title: Eight rules complete
blocks.body: Next: the two checks that catch drafts that still point, and the underside rule that encoding is not permission. Then execution, society, and art.
